No other people at all: no friends, partners, dates, family, colleagues, gifts, cards, letters or notes for someone.
No creative or craft projects (gifts, decorations, drawings, origami, bracelets) and no self-improvement plans (workout routines, budgets, resumes, schedules).

Prefer a question about how a device, material or physical process works or behaves, or about a single maintenance, settings or care check on one object (for example: the difference between a reboot and a reset; why a battery drains; how to unstick a key; whether to fold or roll clothes).
Keep it to one short question: do not ask for a full tutorial, a material list or numbered steps, and do not say you are a beginner.

For friendship and dating, exercise and hobbies, career and job hunting, and personal finance, choose the most object-centred, impersonal angle (an app setting, care of a piece of equipment, a file format, a receipt or card reader), never a person or a plan.
Plain questions: ask one short factual or diagnostic question about the object (what is the difference between X and Y, why does X happen, how can I tell whether X), not a request for a procedure.
